thread:
maria: heads up — after the v1.12.3 release we see a p95 tail spike on shortseq workloads (seq <= 16). rolling canary flagged it this morning :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deployed release v1.12.3 to prod (canary: 10%).

jon: reproable locally? if so, can you paste the minimal repro command?

maria: yes. cheap repro: run the shortseq bench on the canary build. quick command i used:
```
# reproduce locally
python tools/bench.py --model redwood/gpt-small --seq-len 8 --batch-size 1 --quant fused --rps 50
```
results: p95 jumps ~2.8x vs build from yesterday. p50 fine.

sam: sounds like a kernel chooser fallback. any kernel logs?

maria: grabbed traces from canary host. sampling shows a ton of calls to attn_generic after the merge, even though attn_fused_quant_v2 should handle these short sequences and be faster. snippet from host logs:
```
[2026-03-18 09:11:47] kernel_chooser.cpp: select_kernel(model=attn, seq=8, batch=1) -> attn_fused_quant_v2
[2026-03-18 09:11:47] kernel_chooser.cpp: invocation 1 -> attn_fused_quant_v2 (est=0.18s)
[2026-03-18 09:11:47] kernel_chooser.cpp: invocation 2 -> fallback_to(attn_generic) reason=latency_estimate_miscompare
[2026-03-18 09:11:47] runtime_metrics.cpp: fallback_count(attn_fused_quant_v2)=98/120
```

lisa: miscompare as in the estimator is returning higher than actual? could be the calibration change in #2941.

kevin: i ran a small profiler (pprof) on the canary: flame shows attn_generic dominating tail. perf summary:
```
attn_fused_quant_v2: 0.24s (hot path when chosen)
attn_generic: 0.62s (when chosen, much larger latency for short seq)
```

sam: so the chooser is sometimes switching away from fused quant and hitting generic, increasing p95. why would chooser flip? estimator inputs changed recently to use median_latency instead of mean for shortseq heuristic (PR 2941?).

jon: PR 2941 introduced a smoothing window of 100 samples but also eliminated warmup correction for seq <= 16. guessing the estimator initially underestimates, then overcompensates and flips.

maria: timeline: merged PR 2941 two nights ago, canary rolled 6h ago, spike observed 2h after roll. CI perf job did not fail but noise was high on shortseq tests yesterday.

perf-ci: perf-ci: perf/job/shortseq-p95 reported +28% in nightly run (job 2026-03-17-22). tolerance not exceeded so it passed.

kevin: i started a bisect locally across the last 10 commits. early signal points to commit abc1234 (kernel chooser refactor). that commit removed the ceil-to-batch fallback cost adjustment.

lisa: if commit abc1234 removed ceil-to-batch cost, then the estimator may undercount the overhead for very small batches causing unstable decisions. that fits.

sam: two quick mitigation options: 1) immediate canary hold + revert abc1234, or 2) patch chooser to restore small-batch warmup correction (hotfix). which do we prefer?

maria: recommend hotfix first if it's small. we want minimal blast radius. can we ship a revert if hotfix takes too long? yes.

jon: i have a one-line revert candidate and a 3-line hotfix branch that reintroduces the warmup correction math. i can open both PRs now.

maria: open both and mark canary hold. i'll ask infra to freeze rollout.

jon: PRs opened: #3012 (revert abc1234) and #3013 (chooser-warmup-readd). both flagged as hotfix.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for v1.12.3 (reason: manual hold by @maria).

sam: test plan: run shortseq bench + perf-ci quick job with 3 repeats for both PRs. we should also add a stress bench that alternates seq len 8/64 to catch oscillation.

kevin: i ran PR3013 build locally. quick bench shows p95 back to baseline for 2k samples. looks promising.

maria: thumbs up. sam, can you trigger perf-ci quick job on #3013?

sam: kicking off perf job now: perf-ci/quick/3013-run1. ETA ~8m.

perf-ci: perf-ci: quick job completed. shortseq p95 delta -2% vs baseline (n=3).

maria: great — let's promote #3013 to canary patch and resume rollout slowly. keep #3012 as fallback if anything else pops.

jon: will cut canary build with #3013 and bump canary to 30% for 30m then 60% if stable.

lisa: follow-up: add a unit test in chooser that asserts stable decision after warmup window for seq <= 16. and add a perf CI alert to catch >15% p95 regressions on shortseq.

maria: noted. i'll open a follow-up ticket for the test/alert. ticket 4987.

kevin: logs/traces attached to PR3013 for postmortem. main root cause summary: estimator smoothing change removed tiny-batch warmup correction in abc1234, causing decision thrash and fallback to slower generic attn kernel on shortseq bursts.

maria: closing loop: canary promoted, p95 stabilized. leaving canary watch open for 2h. thanks everyone :tada:
